definition: Student counseling is support offered to students, especially in school-based programs, to help with mental health concerns such as stress and related emotional difficulties. In this context, it is presented as part of school efforts to improve adolescent mental health outcomes.

reasons: The packet supports student counseling as a school-based intervention, but it does not explicitly support the added gloss “related emotional difficulties.”

The definition presents student counseling as a general form of support for students; the packet only mentions it as one recommended intervention in school-based programs, not as a full definitional description.

The packet does not define “student counseling” or describe what it involves as “support offered to students” beyond stating that school-based programs should “offer interventions such as stress management and student counseling.”

The definition’s phrasing “to help with mental health concerns such as stress and related emotional difficulties” is only partially supported: the packet mentions stress management, but it does not explicitly mention “related emotional difficulties.”

The packet supports the general idea that school-based programs should address adolescent mental health (and mentions “positive parenting practices” and “school-based programs”), but the definition’s claim that student counseling is “presented as part of school efforts to improve adolescent mental health outcomes” is not stated with that exact characterization.
